Welcome from the Headteacher
I am delighted to welcome you to Henry Green Primary School. At Henry Green, we are more than just a school – we are a family. Every child is valued, cared for, and encouraged to thrive both academically and personally.
Our vision is for children to feel safe, happy, and inspired, knowing that they belong and can achieve their very best. Through high expectations, nurturing relationships, and a broad, engaging curriculum, we aim to equip every child with the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need for life.
We believe in the power of community. Staff, families, and children work together to create an environment where kindness, respect, and perseverance are at the heart of everything we do.
I hope our website gives you a sense of who we are and what we stand for. If you would like to experience our school in action, we would be delighted to welcome you for a visit.

British Values at Henry Green
At Henry Green, British Values are not taught as an add-on, they are lived through our ASPIRE values (Achieve, Succeed, Persevere, Inspire, Respect, Enjoy) and embedded in our IDEAS curriculum.
We want our children to grow up understanding their place in modern Britain, ready to contribute positively to their community and beyond.
We teach children that British Values help to bind us together as a country. They guide how we live, learn and work alongside others. Children are taught to value and respect differences, while also cherishing what we have in common.
How we share British Values at Henry Green:
Our IDEAS curriculum is carefully designed to prepare children for life in modern Britain. Through topics such as World War II, The Tudors, The Great Fire of London, Ancient Greece and Local Area Studies, children explore democracy, laws, liberty, respect and tolerance in meaningful contexts.
Through assemblies we bring British Values to life. We use stories, events and celebrations to connect with our ASPIRE values, and we encourage children to reflect on fairness, respect and responsibility.
In PSHE, children learn about their rights, responsibilities and personal freedoms, as well as how to keep themselves and others safe. Mutual respect is at the heart of this learning, and children are encouraged to celebrate differences and value friendships.
Through the Barking and Dagenham syllabus, children gain a deeper understanding of different faiths, beliefs and worldviews. This promotes respect and tolerance for others, both locally and globally.
PE provides opportunities for teamwork, fair play and respect. Children learn how to win graciously, cope with defeat and support others, both in lessons and in wider sporting opportunities.
Our School Parliament is a real example of democracy in action. Children are elected by their peers to represent pupil voice and contribute to decision-making in school. This helps every child to understand that their voice matters and can make a difference.British Values at Henry Green

pageCache.text:
I am delighted to welcome you to the Henry Green School website.
At Henry Green, we are more than just a school, we are a family.
We are a place where every child and adult feels safe, valued, and inspired to learn and flourish.
Our brain-based approach, combined with care, connection and high expectations, creates a nurturing and ambitious community where everyone is known, supported and challenged to be their very best—not just for today, but for life.
Learning Together, Learning for Life.
Our Core Values – ASPIRE
Our ASPIRE values shape everything we do. They guide how we learn, how we treat one another, and how we grow — together — as a school family.
Achieve – We help every child achieve their personal best.
Succeed – We celebrate success and believe every child can succeed.
Persevere – We face challenges with courage and resilience.
Inspire – We nurture curiosity, creativity and ambition.
Respect – We treat everyone with kindness, empathy and respect.
Enjoy – We create happy memories and enjoy learning together.
We have two forms of entry from Reception through to year 6 and a nursery, providing education for children from 3-11. We hope that our website gives you all the information you need about our school.
We are always pleased to welcome visitors so please make an appointment at the school’s main office should you wish to come and visit.
Ms H Daley Headteacher

Music at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, music is more than a subject; it’s a powerful form of expression, connection and creativity. Regardless of ability, race, culture or religion, music brings everyone together. It gives every child the chance to participate, communicate and shine.
We believe in fostering a lifelong love of music, helping children build confidence, celebrate diversity and develop the creative and collaborative skills they need for the future.
Our music curriculum reflects the needs of our community and is underpinned by our ASPIRE values, our IDEAS framework and the Charanga scheme of work. We aim to ensure that every child has the opportunity to experience, enjoy and excel in music, regardless of background or ability.
Our music curriculum is shaped by our IDEAS principles:
All children are musicians. We ensure that every child, including those with SEND or EAL, can participate fully in music lessons. Charanga’s adaptive design and our inclusive ethos ensure that every pupil can access, enjoy and achieve music.
Musical learning is carefully sequenced to revisit and build on knowledge over time. Pupils explore key concepts like rhythm, pitch, tempo, structure and dynamics with increasing depth. They reflect on their work, analyse performances and use feedback to refine and improve.
Music is exciting, hands-on and joyful. Pupils immerse themselves in a wide range of musical styles, traditions and cultures — from classical and jazz to pop and world music. They are encouraged to take creative risks and enjoy ownership over what they compose and perform.
We make music real. Children experience music through meaningful performance opportunities, use real instruments and make links to their own lives and communities. They understand how music reflects identity, tells stories and shapes history.
Music helps children develop confidence, communication, collaboration, resilience and self-expression, kills they will use well beyond the classroom. Pupils leave Henry Green with a lasting love of music and a strong foundation for further musical learning and enjoyment.
Curriculum Implementation
At Henry Green, music is taught weekly using the Charanga Musical School Scheme, supported by enriching experiences and opportunities throughout the year.
Our approach includes:
Music learning begins in EYFS, where children develop musical awareness through singing, movement, rhymes and exploration. As they move through the school, children gain more control and independence over their musical choices and performances.
Our thorough approach allows pupils to think deeply about their work — to analyse, evaluate, reflect and refine. This develops not just musical skill but a rich understanding of music as an expressive art form.
Music at Henry Green nurtures not only creativity, but emotional well-being, independence and identity — empowering pupils to discover their voice and share it with pride.
We Enrich Music Learning with:
These experiences bring music to life and help children develop confidence, creativity and a love of performing. They deepen pupils’ understanding of musical genres, traditions and careers, allowing them to connect their learning to the wider world and future opportunities.
At Henry Green, we see the impact of our music curriculum in happy, motivated learners who are confident to explore and express themselves through sound.
We know our music curriculum is successful when:
We measure impact through:
At Henry Green, we proudly uphold this belief. Music is woven into the fabric of school life, giving every child a voice, a sense of belonging and the inspiration to fly.

Art and Design at Henry Green
At Henry Green, Art and Design is a vital part of our creative family. It gives every child the opportunity to express themselves, explore their imagination and celebrate their individuality. Through a rich and inclusive curriculum, we nurture curiosity, develop artistic skills and encourage children to take pride in their ideas. Art and Design at Henry Green supports personal growth and prepares children to engage confidently with the world around them.
Art and Design Curriculum Intent
At Henry Green, our Art and Design curriculum reflects the creativity, diversity, and individuality of our school community. Rooted in our ASPIRE values and delivered through the Kapow Primary scheme, it provides all children with the opportunity to explore, express, and develop their artistic skills and confidence.
Aligned with the National Curriculum and guided by our IDEAS principles, Art and Design is:

Our aim is for every child to see themselves as an artist, to value creativity, and to leave Henry Green with the ability to appreciate, critique, and create art with confidence and purpose.
Art and Design Curriculum Implementation
At Henry Green, Art and Design is delivered through high-quality teaching, inspiring experiences, and strong teacher-pupil relationships that foster creativity and confidence.
Art and Design is monitored and supported by a subject lead who works closely with staff to ensure high standards of delivery. Ongoing professional development, reflective practice, and a commitment to inclusion and excellence ensure that every child at Henry Green can enjoy and achieve in Art and Design.

Inclusion in Art and Design
Art and Design is accessible to all. We use a range of strategies and resources to meet the needs of every child, including those with SEND. Lessons are adapted with sensory-friendly materials, visual aids, and adult support where needed, ensuring every child can fully participate, express themselves, and succeed creatively.

Every child has the right to reliable information from a variety of sources.
Reading at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, reading is at the heart of our curriculum and the key to unlocking every child’s potential. We believe that reading transforms lives — it opens minds, builds confidence, and connects children to the world around them.
Our reading curriculum is inclusive, ambitious, and rooted in our ASPIRE values. It is designed to ensure that every child becomes a fluent, enthusiastic reader who finds both joy and purpose in books. Through reading, we develop children’s vocabulary, imagination, emotional understanding, and academic success — preparing them for a lifetime of learning.
Our intent is to foster a lifelong love of reading and ensure every child has the tools to become a confident, capable reader.
We expose children to a diverse range of high-quality texts that reflect the world they live in, challenge their thinking, and nurture empathy and curiosity. From early phonics to advanced comprehension, we support all learners – including those with SEND or EAL – to develop strong decoding, fluency, and understanding.
Reading at Henry Green goes beyond meeting curriculum expectations. It builds cultural capital, empowers children with language, and equips them with the skills and mindset they need to thrive.
Our IDEAS Approach to Reading:
Every child is supported to succeed in reading. We remove barriers through structured phonics, adaptive teaching, visual supports, and a rich range of accessible, diverse texts. Every child – regardless of background or need -can see themselves as a reader.
D – Deepening the Learning
Reading is carefully sequenced and revisited to build fluency, comprehension, and critical thinking. We use the VIPERS framework (Vocabulary, Inference, Prediction, Explanation, Retrieval, and Summarising) and a rich reading spine to deepen understanding over time.
Reading is exciting and purposeful. From daily story time to whole-class discussions, role-play, and book-based projects, we immerse children in texts that spark imagination and reflect real life. When reading is enjoyable, it sticks.
Children read real books for real reasons. Our texts explore meaningful themes and lived experiences, allowing children to connect their reading to the wider world. Reading isn’t confined to English lessons — it lives throughout the curriculum.
S – Securing Future Success
Fluent, thoughtful readers are ready for the future. Our curriculum equips children with comprehension skills, analytical thinking, and a love of reading that prepares them for secondary school and beyond.
Curriculum Implementation
At Henry Green, reading is taught daily and prioritised across the curriculum. We use a systematic and rigorous approach to ensure all children make strong progress from the start. Early Reading and Phonics
We follow Read Write Inc. Phonics, delivered with fidelity, consistency, and ambition. Children are taught in small groups matched to their stage of learning, and progress is reviewed every half term.
Decodable texts are carefully matched to phonics knowledge to build confidence and fluency. Children who need extra support receive daily 1:1 or small group tutoring to keep up.
Reading Across the School
As children move beyond phonics, we develop comprehension and fluency through:
Children are immersed in language-rich environments, with inviting book corners, reading displays, and libraries that reflect different cultures, experiences, and authors. We celebrate reading through events such as World Book Day, author visits, reading ambassadors, and family reading sessions — ensuring that reading is a shared, joyful experience for our whole community.
Reading in Key Stages
In Key Stage 1, we focus on securing early reading through phonics and fluency. Sessions are multisensory, practical, and inclusive – with choral reading, storytelling, vocabulary games, and lots of talk to build confidence and understanding.
In Key Stage 2, we teach reading through high-quality whole-class texts. Children develop their comprehension using VIPERS, apply strategies through independent and group tasks, and record their thinking using journals, graphic organisers, and verbal responses.
We continue to ensure flexibility for all learners through scaffolds, visuals, and targeted support.
The impact of our reading curriculum is evident in the way our children read, talk, and think. By the end of Key Stage 2, children at Henry Green:
Children with additional needs also make strong progress. They access reading through tailored approaches and develop the same love and confidence as their peers.
How We Measure Impact:
Reading unlocks learning. It builds self-esteem, knowledge, and connection. At Henry Green, we are proud to grow readers who are not only ready for the next stage of their education – but ready to shape the world around them.
“If you don’t like to read, you haven’t found the right book.” – J.K. Rowling
Writing at Henry Green Primary School
Every child must be free to express their thoughts and opinions and to access all kinds of information, as long as it is within the law.
At Henry Green, we believe that writing is a powerful tool – for communication, creativity, and connection. Writing gives children a voice, builds confidence, and unlocks opportunities both within and beyond the classroom.
Our writing curriculum is grounded in our ASPIRE values and shaped by our IDEAS framework. It is inclusive, inspiring, and ambitious for all learners. Through a carefully sequenced and engaging approach, we support every child to become a capable, confident writer who takes pride in their work and writes with purpose and joy.
Our intent is to develop articulate, reflective writers who can write effectively for a range of audiences and purposes. We aim to nurture every child’s creativity, critical thinking, and ability to express themselves clearly and confidently.
While our writing curriculum fully meets the expectations of the National Curriculum, it goes further. It is rooted in high-quality texts, rich vocabulary, and purposeful writing experiences that support academic success, emotional growth, and future readiness.
We believe every child is a writer and our job is to help them find and develop their voice.
Our IDEAS Approach to Writing:
We remove barriers to writing so that all children – including those with SEND, EAL, or other needs – can succeed. Our teaching is adaptive and supportive, using scaffolding, oral rehearsal, and shared writing to ensure every child can participate fully.
D – Deepening the Learning
Writing is carefully sequenced to build on prior knowledge and develop depth over time. Through the Talk for Writing approach, children internalise structure, develop grammatical control, and craft language with increasing sophistication. Editing and redrafting are central to the process.
Writing is brought to life through drama, discussion, rich texts, and real-world links. From EYFS onwards, we use meaningful hooks and high-quality stimuli to spark imagination and motivation. When learning is engaging, it sticks.
Children write with purpose and for real audiences — from letters and leaflets to poems and persuasive texts. Writing is linked to real issues, curriculum themes, and personal experience, giving children a reason to care about their work.
S – Securing Future Success
Writing is a life skill. Children leave Henry Green with the ability to write fluently, accurately, and creatively. They can adapt their tone and style, communicate effectively, and take pride in their ideas and achievements.
Curriculum Implementation
Writing at Henry Green is taught through the Talk for Writing approach. This provides a consistent, research-based framework built around the three stages of imitation, innovation, and independent application.
We use rich model texts to expose children to ambitious vocabulary, strong sentence structures, and effective authorial techniques. Oral rehearsal, drama, and shared writing support children to internalise language patterns and write confidently from experience.
From the early years onwards, we build writing on a strong foundation of spoken language and phonics. In Key Stage 1, children develop sentence fluency and begin writing for different purposes.
In Key Stage 2, pupils write with increasing independence, applying grammar and punctuation purposefully across a wide range of genres. All classrooms are language-rich, with vocabulary walls, magpie books, and visual supports.
Writing is taught explicitly, but also applied meaningfully across the wider curriculum. Highexpectations, clear modelling, and ongoing feedback help children refine and improve their work.
Subject leaders support staff through training, coaching, and regular monitoring to ensure consistent, high-quality practice across the school. Planning is collaborative and reflective, allowing staff to respond to pupils’ needs while maintaining progression and challenge.
The impact of our writing curriculum is seen in children who write with confidence, creativity, and care.
We know our approach is effective when:
How We Measure Impact:
Writing at Henry Green is not just about meeting standards – it is about helping children find their voice, express their identity, and shape their futures with confidence and pride.
“If you want to be a writer, you must do two things above all others: read a lot and write a lot.” – Stephen King

Every child has the right to learn and use the language, customs and religion of their family, whether or not these are shared by the majority of the people in the country where they live.
MFL at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, our French curriculum, taught through the SALUT scheme, inspires a love of languages and develops key communication skills. SALUT provides fun, structured lessons that build confidence in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. Through cultural exploration and language learning, pupils gain a deeper understanding of the wider world, preparing them for future language study and life as global citizens.
MFL at Henry Green aims to inspire all children to make connections with different people and their cultures and to play a fuller part as global citizens.
Our intention is to provide high-quality language education that allows children to develop their interest in learning other languages in a way that is enjoyable and stimulating. Our MFL curriculum focuses on the progression of second language acquisition where children have the opportunity to speak, read, listen to and write in French.
We aim to encourage children’s curiosity about language and the wider world while teaching them about different parts of France and French speaking countries subsequently developing their awareness of cultural differences in other countries. We strive to embed the skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing necessary to enable children to use and apply their French learning in a variety of contexts and lay the foundations for future language learning.
Our IDEAS Curriculum Framework
Our curriculum is shaped by IDEAS, a set of core principles that guide how we plan and deliver learning:
Children work together to create French dialogue and written work based on topics which reflect on everyday activities for primary school children.
Finding ways of using our language learning outside of school and evaluating sentence structures in English and French.
Learning through fun games, songs, and familiar stories.
Authentic French voices and pronunciation, traditional French stories and songs allowing pupils to experience a different culture.
Opportunities to build on prior learning and improve in all four language skills (Speaking, Reading, Writing, and listening)
Curriculum Implementation
At Henry Green, our MFL curriculum is delivered through the SALUT scheme, providing a clear progression of skills across Key Stage 2. Lessons are designed to build confidence in listening, speaking, reading, and writing French, while fostering cultural awareness and enjoyment. Language is taught weekly by class teachers using consistent resources and engaging approaches.
At Henry Green, the impact of our MFL curriculum is seen in the growing confidence, enthusiasm, and linguistic skills of our pupils. Through the SALUT scheme, children develop a strong foundation in French, preparing them for further language learning and helping them become open-minded, culturally aware individuals.
We know our curriculum is successful when:
How We Measure Impact
At Henry Green, we use a range of strategies to measure the impact of our MFL curriculum and ensure pupils are making good progress in their language learning.
These methods help us evaluate how well pupils are developing their French language skills and cultural awareness. They also inform future planning and support targeted interventions to ensure all learners achieve success.

Every child has the right to a standard of living adequate for their physical, mental, spiritual, moral and social development.
Geography at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, geography inspires children to explore and understand the world around them, its places, people, environments, and how they are all connected. We want our pupils to think like geographers by asking thoughtful questions, using maps and data, investigating real-world issues, and developing a sense of place and responsibility.
Through our exciting curriculum, children gain a deeper awareness of both their local area and the wider world, becoming curious, caring, and informed global citizens.
Our Geography will incite children’s curiosity and fascination about the world and provide answers to questions about the natural and human aspects of the world. Children are encouraged to develop a greater understanding and knowledge of the world. We are committed to providing children with opportunities to investigate and make enquiries about their local area so that they can develop of real sense of who they are, their heritage and what makes our local area unique and special.
Geography at Henry Green is shaped by our IDEAS framework:
Geography at our school is inclusive and representative of all learners. Topics and materials are chosen to reflect the geographical backgrounds/heritage of our diverse community and to our children ability and needs. Lessons are carefully planned with clear modelling, visual aids, and practical activities to help all children engage with geographical concepts.
In geography, learning is deepened by encouraging children to ask questions, investigate patterns, and draw conclusions from real-world data and experiences. They build on prior knowledge through progressively challenging topics and make connections between local and global issues to develop a thorough understanding of the world around them.
Powerful stimuluses – WOW! moments and Big Finishers, together with fieldwork help engage and inspire pupils
Authentic learning experiences based around our local area and our community heritage feeds into the geography curriculum.
Geography equips children with essential skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, and effective communication, which are vital for their future education and careers. By fostering a deeper understanding of people and places, our curriculum prepares pupils to become responsible global citizens who can navigate and positively impact an ever-changing world.
Curriculum Implementation
We follow the Kapow curriculum from Reception to Year 6. Our Geography curriculum is implemented using Kapow Primary, which provides a clear, well-structured progression of lessons designed to build knowledge and skills systematically.
Geography lessons at Henry Green are:
We use a spiral curriculum approach in geography, meaning key concepts and skills are revisited and built upon over time, deepening pupils’ understanding as they progress through the school.

We use both formative and summative assessment to measure progress and inform teaching:

Children have the right to reliable information from a variety of sources.
History at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, history is an exciting journey through time where children explore the lives, events, and cultures that have shaped the world we live in today. We want our pupils to think like historians—asking questions, examining evidence, making connections, and developing a deep understanding of cause and consequence.
Through an engaging curriculum, children gain a sense of identity and curiosity about the past, helping them become thoughtful, informed citizens of the future.
Our history will inspire pupils’ curiosity to know more about the past in order to shape their future and equip the children to ask perceptive questions, think critically, analyse evidence. It will help pupils to understand the process of change, the diversity of societies as well as their own identity and the challenges of their time. It is aligned with the National Curriculum and the Kapow scheme, but goes further – providing a sense of wonder, empathy and an appreciation for how the past continues to influence the present.
History at Henry Green is shaped by our IDEAS framework:
History at our school is inclusive and representative of all learners. We ensure that pupils explore a diverse range of people, cultures, and perspectives from the past, including voices that have often been underrepresented. We are committed to ensuring that all pupils are supported to access and enjoy. Lessons are carefully planned with clear modelling, visual aids, and practical activities to help all children engage with historical concepts.
Children’s learning is deepened through the use of enquiry-based questions, revisiting key concepts over time, and making meaningful connections across topics. Children are encouraged to explore cause and consequence, compare periods, and reflect on continuity and change to develop a richer, more secure understanding of the past.
Powerful stimuluses – WOW! moments and Big Finishers, together with visits to historically significant places help engage and inspire pupils.
Authentic learning experiences based around our local history in every year group and our school context feeds into the history curriculum.
History helps secure future success by developing critical thinking, curiosity, and a strong sense of identity. Through learning how to question evidence, understand different perspectives, and communicate ideas clearly, children build valuable skills that prepare them for further learning and life beyond the classroom.
Curriculum Implementation
We follow the Kapow curriculum from Reception to Year 6. Our history curriculum is delivered through Kapow Primary, offering a carefully sequenced and comprehensive approach that builds children’s knowledge and historical skills progressively.
History lessons at Henry Green are:
We use a spiral curriculum approach in history, meaning key concepts and skills are revisited and built upon over time, deepening pupils’ understanding as they progress through the school.
Beyond the Classroom
We enrich history learning with:
These experiences help children see history in action and connect learning to their lives and future choices.
Assessment in History
We use both formative and summative assessment to measure progress and inform teaching:
Assessment is inclusive and flexible, with varied outcomes (verbal, practical, written) to reflect every child’s strengths. Gaps are identified early so we can plan effective next steps.
The impact of our history curriculum is evident in the way our children talk, think, and behave like historians.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils:
Children with additional needs also make meaningful progress. They can access, engage with, and succeed in history through assessable content and scaffolding. artefacts, videos, role play, drawing timelines, and practical investigations, which benefit learners who need concrete, visual or hands-on learning.

Every child has the right to an education.
Mathematics at Henry Green
At Henry Green, we believe every child is a mathematician — capable of reasoning, problem-solving, and making sense of the world through numbers.
Our maths curriculum builds confident learners who can apply mathematical knowledge with curiosity, creativity, and resilience. We want every child to leave our school with a secure understanding of mathematics and a belief in their own ability to succeed.
Rooted in our ASPIRE values and guided by our IDEAS principles, we aim to foster a deep understanding of mathematical concepts through a curriculum that is inclusive, engaging, and aspirational.
Our maths curriculum reflects our belief that all children can achieve in mathematics. Aligned with the National Curriculum and delivered through the White Rose Maths (WRM) scheme, it provides rich, carefully sequenced learning that is inclusive, ambitious, and meaningful.
Mathematics at Henry Green is shaped by our IDEAS framework:
All learners access high-quality mathematical experiences. Our curriculum scaffolds learning through C-P-A (Concrete – Pictorial – Abstract) while offering stretch and challenge for all.
Adaptive teaching and support ensure that every child can engage meaningfully in maths. D – Deepening the Learning Concepts are introduced and revisited through a structured rogression of small steps, supporting long-term retention and deep understanding.
We use the WRM calculation policy to ensure continuity and coherence in how children learn to calculate and reason mathematically.
Our lessons are purposeful and stimulating, using real-life contexts and practical resources to spark curiosity and develop critical thinking. We nurture enjoyment and confidence in maths from the early years through to Year 6.
We make maths relevant to children’s lives. Whether calculating time in a real-world context, budgeting in a class project, or exploring patterns in nature, we help children see the value and purpose of mathematics.
S – Securing Future Success
From subitising in EYFS to algebra and reasoning in Year 6, our curriculum provides the knowledge and skills needed for secondary school and beyond. Pupils leave Henry Green numerate, reflective and able to apply their understanding in diverse contexts.
We follow the White Rose Maths scheme from Nursery to Year 6. This provides a structured, coherent progression through all strands of the National Curriculum, including number, operations, geometry, measurement and statistics.
Our teaching approach includes:
By the time our children leave Henry Green, they are equipped with not just secure number knowledge and calculation skills, but the ability to think logically, solve problems creatively, and approach challenges with confidence and resilience.
EYFS and Key Stage 1
Children explore maths through songs, stories, manipulatives and practical activities. We focus on number sense, subitising, number bonds and early problem-solving. Maths is taught daily in short, engaging sessions, with learning captured through observation and talk.
Children develop formal written methods alongside mental strategies. They apply learning to more complex problems, including fractions, decimals and percentages. Lessons include regular opportunities for reasoning, discussion and collaborative problem-solving.
Maths is for everyone. We use scaffolds, adapted models, practical resources, and adult support to meet the needs of every child. Adaptive teaching ensures that all pupils including those with SEND or EAL — can access learning and achieve success.
Beyond the Classroom
Maths is celebrated across our school through:
These experiences help children connect classroom learning to the world around them.
We use formative and summative assessments to track progress and inform planning:
Assessment is inclusive and varied, ensuring every child’s progress is recognised and supported.
By the end of Key Stage 2, our pupils:
Children with additional needs make meaningful progress, developing mathematical understanding in ways that suit their individual learning profiles.

pageCache.text:
Every child has the right to rest and leisure, to engage in play and recreational activities appropriate to the age of the child.
At Henry Green, we believe that physical education is about much more than sport. Our PE curriculum promotes physical health, teamwork, confidence and resilience — all of which help children to thrive both in and out of the classroom.
Our approach to PE is shaped by our IDEAS framework:
Every child, regardless of ability, background or need, is supported to enjoy and succeed in physical activity. We adapt lessons to ensure all pupils can participate fully and confidently.
Skills are taught progressively across year groups, with children building strength, control, and understanding over time. We revisit and refine core techniques across a range of sports and movement activities.
Lessons are energetic, purposeful and fun. We use PE Passport to plan high-quality, varied experiences that motivate children to be active and try new things.
PE is rooted in real-world contexts. We make links to history, geography, art and design where possible (e.g. dance through time, sports from around the world, movement inspired by visual art), helping pupils understand the cultural, social and creative relevance of physical activity.
Curriculum Implementation
PE at Henry Green is taught through a carefully sequenced, high-quality programme using the PE Passport platform, which supports planning, progression and assessment across the school.
Our PE curriculum has a clear impact on children’s physical development, self-confidence, and personal wellbeing. We know it is successful when:
We measure impact through:
At Henry Green, PE is about building confident movers, healthy minds, and strong team players — children who are active now and ready for lifelong wellbeing.

Every child has the right to say what they think in all matters affecting them, and to have their views taken seriously.
At Henry Green, Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education is central to our commitment to children’s wellbeing and personal growth. We see PSHE as the foundation for helping children to flourish, both in school and in their lives beyond. Through carefully planned lessons, assemblies and whole-school initiatives, pupils learn how to look after themselves, build positive relationships, and develop the skills needed to become confident, responsible and caring members of society. PSHE reflects our ethos — every child is supported, valued and empowered to thrive.
Our PSHE curriculum equips children with the knowledge, skills and attitudes they need to thrive in the modern world. We want our pupils to be healthy, safe, resilient and respectful individuals who make positive contributions to their community and beyond. Through PSHE, children learn how to develop healthy relationships, manage their feelings, understand themselves and others, and make informed choices.
Our curriculum is built on the Jigsaw scheme of work, enhanced with MindUp (Goldie Hawn Foundation) and our Interoception curriculum, ensuring that children’s emotional regulation and wellbeing are embedded alongside their personal development.
We align our PSHE teaching with our whole-school IDEAS framework:
Every child sees themselves reflected in the curriculum and feels valued, respected and safe.
Children build a strong understanding of themselves and others, developing lifelong strategies for wellbeing, relationships and resilience.
Lessons are practical, meaningful and connected to real-life experiences, ensuring children can apply their learning.
Children learn skills and knowledge that prepare them for real challenges and opportunities, both now and in the future.
PSHE provides the foundation for children’s health, happiness, safety and ability to thrive in society.
At Henry Green, we prioritise PSHE as part of our dedication to children’s wellbeing. Every Monday morning begins with a PSHE lesson across the school, providing a soft start to the week and giving children time to settle, reflect and prepare for their learning after the weekend.
Our curriculum is rooted in the Jigsaw scheme, which provides a progressive, spiral curriculum covering the six key themes: Being Me in My World, Celebrating Difference, Dreams and Goals, Healthy Me, Relationships and Changing Me. These themes are revisited and built upon year on year to ensure consistency and progression for all pupils.
To complement this, we use the MindUp programme, where short “brain breaks” are built into the school day — at the start of the morning, after break and after lunch — helping children to regulate, calm their thinking and be ready to learn. Alongside this, our Interoception curriculum supports children in recognising and responding to their internal body signals (such as hunger, tiredness or anxiety), strengthening their emotional awareness and self-regulation.
PSHE is also woven throughout school life, from assemblies and circle times to wider initiatives such as Anti-Bullying Week, Safer Internet Day and our work as a Rights Respecting Gold School. All lessons are delivered in a safe and inclusive environment, where respect, listening and kindness are central, giving children the confidence to share their ideas and feelings. Staff are trained in trauma-informed and emotionally available approaches, ensuring that our provision is sensitive, consistent and responsive to children’s needs.
Through our PSHE curriculum, children at Henry Green will:
We measure impact through pupil voice, learning walks, book looks and by observing how children apply their learning in daily school life. The ultimate measure of impact is seen in confident, caring and responsible pupils who are ready for the next stage of their education and for life beyond Henry Green.

Every child has the right to think and believe what they choose and to practise their religion.
Religious Education at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, Religious Education (RE) is more than a subject — it’s a vital part of our whole-child approach. Through RE, we develop pupils’ understanding of themselves and others, helping them to become thoughtful, respectful citizens of a diverse world.
We create a safe and inclusive space where children of all backgrounds feel valued, heard, and empowered to explore big questions about life, beliefs and values.
Our Religious Education curriculum reflects the diversity of our community and is underpinned by our ASPIRE values, the Barking and Dagenham Agreed Syllabus and a strong belief that every child can succeed in school and in life.
We aim to give all pupils:
Our RE curriculum encourages every pupil to develop a sense of identity, purpose, and belonging, preparing them to contribute positively to our multicultural society.
Our RE curriculum is guided by the same IDEAS principles that shape learning across the school:
Religious Education is open to all. It promotes an inclusive environment that meets the needs of all pupils, irrespective of age, disability, race, religion, belief or gender by creating a respectful environment where pupils of different backgrounds can freely discuss sensitive topics and challenge prejudice without facing judgement .We celebrate and explore a wide range of beliefs, ensuring every child feels represented and respected.
Lessons are carefully sequenced to build on prior knowledge and revisit key concepts. Pupils analyse, justify and evaluate their perspectives on ethical and philosophical questions, thereby developing important skills of critical thinking and reflecting deeply on religion and worldviews.
We bring RE to life through rich experiences — stories, artefacts, drama, music, video, festivals, visits to places of worship and speakers from different faiths. These memorable experiences help children connect emotionally and intellectually with their learning. Pupils have confidence in their own growing sense of identity and empower the religious and non-religious through inquiry.
Learning is connected to children’s own experiences and the world around them. Artefacts, videos, visits to place of worship and various cultural and religious practices establish a sense of reality and give weight to what is discussed in lessons.
Prior learning is constantly referred to so that pupils build upon existing ideas and enrich themselves with new information in order to secure skills and knowledge in their long-term memory. Pupils develop empathy, communication skills, resilience and critical thinking — essential qualities for future learning and life in a diverse world.
Curriculum Implementation
Religious Education is taught weekly following the Barking and Dagenham Agreed Syllabus, Lessons are interactive, reflective and thoughtfully planned to meet the needs of all learners.
Children explore key themes such as special people, books, celebrations, places and objects, using these as entry points into broader learning about identity, community, morality, and belief. Our classrooms are inclusive spaces where children can express themselves, ask questions, and learn from each other.
The RE subject leader works closely with staff to support planning, provide training and monitor teaching and learning to ensure consistency and high standards across the school
Inclusion in Religious Education
We are committed to ensuring that all children, including those with SEND, can fully access and engage with learning. Teachers carefully plan and scaffold tasks to match the needs and abilities of each pupil, using a range of approaches such as open-ended tasks, differentiated activities and tasks with increasing complexity. Resources are adapted to suit different levels of understanding and additional adult support is provided when needed to help individuals or small groups. We also consider the language demands of RE lessons, providing targeted support for pupils with English as an additional language to help them develop both their religious understanding and language skills. This inclusive approach ensures that every child can participate meaningfully and confidently in their RE learning.
RE is enriched through:
These experiences bring RE to life, helping children explore beliefs and values in meaningful contexts. They promote respect, curiosity and understanding and help pupils connect learning to their own lives, identity, and the diverse world around them.
Assessment in Religious Education
We use both formative and summative assessment to measure progress and inform teaching in RE:
Assessment in RE is inclusive and flexible, allowing for a variety of responses, verbal, written, creative, or practical, to reflect each child’s strengths and beliefs. Teachers assess not only knowledge of religions and worldviews but also pupils’ ability to reflect, empathise, and think critically. Gaps in understanding are identified early to guide planning and support meaningful progress for all learners.
The impact of the RE curriculum is seen as children become reflective, respectful and deeply curious about the world and the people in it.
We know our RE curriculum is effective when:
How We Measure Impact:
At Henry Green, Religious Education helps shape children who are kind, confident, and ready to make a positive difference in the world. They leave us not only with knowledge of belief systems but with a deep respect for others and the courage to be themselves.

Every child has the right to an education.
Science at Henry Green Primary School
At Henry Green, we believe that every child is a natural scientist – full of curiosity, questions, and wonder. Our science curriculum nurtures that curiosity and equips children with the knowledge and skills they need to explore, understand, and care for the world around them.
We want every child to think like a scientist, ask big questions, and grow into a confident, responsible learner who sees their role in shaping a better future.
Our science curriculum reflects our belief that children learn best when they feel safe, inspired, and challenged. It is aligned with the National Curriculum and the White Rose Science scheme, but goes further – providing rich, hands-on experiences that are meaningful, inclusive, and memorable.
Science at Henry Green is shaped by our IDEAS framework:
All children can succeed in science. We remove barriers and provide carefully adapted learning so every child, including those with SEND, can develop scientific understanding.
D – Deepening the Learning
Children build secure, connected knowledge over time. They revisit and apply key concepts, ask questions, and draw on scientific theories to solve real-world problems.
Learning through fun games, songs, and familiar stories.
Science is purposeful. Children direct their own investigations, work with real scientific equipment, and link learning to the world around them.
S – Securing Future Sucess
Through sustainability and environmental topics, children consider their impact on the world and begin to see themselves as responsible, informed global citizens.
Science enables our children to develop critical thinking, confidence, and curiosity – building the foundation they need to succeed at secondary school and beyond.
Curriculum Implementation
We follow the White Rose Science curriculum from Reception to Year 6. This carefully sequenced scheme provides full coverage of the National Curriculum while also exploring wider global issues such as sustainability and environmental impact.
Science lessons at Henry Green are:
We regularly revisit key ideas through retrieval tasks and discussions, helping children connect prior and new learning.
Science in Key Stages
In Key Stage 1, we follow a Universal Design for Learning (UDL) approach to ensure science is fully accessible and developmentally appropriate for all children. Lessons are practical, hands-on, and exploratory, allowing pupils to engage through talk, play, investigation, and sensory experiences. Children do not use science books at this stage – instead, learning is captured through observations, photographs, and verbal explanations.
In Key Stage 2, we continue to build on this practical, inclusive approach while gradually introducing more opportunities for children to record their learning in books. This includes written reflections, labelled diagrams, or results from investigations – always with flexibility to meet individual needs.
Our aim is to maintain a balance between active, enquiry-based learning and age-appropriate recording that supports knowledge retention and scientific thinking.
Beyond the Classroom
We enrich science learning with:
These experiences help children see science in action and connect learning to their lives and future choices.
Assessment in Science
We use both formative and summative assessment to measure progress and inform teaching:
Assessment is inclusive and flexible, with varied outcomes (verbal, practical, written) to reflect every child’s strengths. Gaps are identified early so we can plan effective next steps.
The impact of our science curriculum is evident in the way our children talk, think, and behave like scientists.
By the end of Key Stage 2, pupils:
Children with additional needs also make meaningful progress. They access science in a way that suits their learning profile — through sensory exploration, simplified concepts, or hands-on experiences — and develop the same sense of wonder and confidence as their peers.
“The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existing.” – Albert Einstein
